Paragraph line spacing: Use python-docx paragraph_format.line_spacing to read spacing values; double spacing can be represented as a float multiplier (e.g., 2.0) or as a fixed Pt value, so check both the value and line_spacing_rule attribute when comparing

When comparing per-paragraph line spacing between a result doc and a gold doc, iterate zip(doc1.paragraphs, doc2.paragraphs) and assert spacing equality for each pair; also verify paragraph counts match first

Line spacing set via LibreOffice UI may be stored differently than via python-docx API (rule WD_LINE_SPACING.DOUBLE vs numeric 2.0), so gold files may come in two variants — use an 'or' conjunction across both gold references when evaluating
Use python-docx paragraph_format.line_spacing and line_spacing_rule properties to verify spacing; compare across paragraphs using zip on non-empty paragraph lists
Use python-docx paragraph_format.line_spacing to read spacing values; compare per-paragraph between result and reference documents using zip(doc1.paragraphs, doc2.paragraphs).
Line spacing values in python-docx can be a float multiplier (e.g., 2.0 for double) or a Pt/Emu length for exact spacing; check the type before comparing.
Paragraph count equality must be verified before per-paragraph spacing comparison to avoid false positives from mismatched structure.
Tab stops (alignment and position): Use python-docx paragraph_format.tab_stops to retrieve tab stop objects; each has .alignment (WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT enum) and .position (EMU integer) properties
Filter out CLEAR and default LEFT-at-0 tab stops before comparing, as these are noise entries not set by the user
Compare tab stop alignment equality directly; for position, compute relative difference against paragraph width (page_width minus margins) to get a normalized score rather than exact match
Verify paragraph text is split by '\t' and check word counts in each segment to confirm the tab character is actually inserted in the text
paragraph_width = section.page_width - section.left_margin - section.right_margin is the correct denominator for normalizing position differences
Subscript text formatting: Use python-docx `run.font.subscript` (bool) to check whether a run has subscript formatting applied; iterate paragraph runs to find the target run.
The `compare_subscript_contains` pattern checks that at least one paired run in both documents has `font.subscript == True`, confirming the property is set rather than just visually similar text.
Page numbers in footers: Use python-docx Document.sections to iterate sections; check section.footer.paragraphs for presence of digit characters as a proxy for a page-number field (PAGE fields render as digits after save/reload).

python-docx does not expose OoxmlElement PAGE fields as plain text; after saving from LibreOffice the field value may appear as a digit string in paragraph.text, so checking any(char.isdigit() for char in footer_text) is a reliable heuristic.
Footer alignment (left/center/right) can be inspected via paragraph.alignment on footer.paragraphs[0]; tab stops in the footer style distinguish left vs. center vs. right placement.
Font name (typeface) applied to text run: Use python-docx: iterate doc.paragraphs → paragraph.runs and check run.font.name for each run; a run with font.name == None may inherit the default theme font rather than an explicit override, so treat None as a potential mismatch when a specific font is required

When a font is applied 'throughout the document', every run in every paragraph must carry the explicit font name — paragraph-level or document-default styles are not reflected in run.font.name, so per-run checking is the correct strategy
python-docx's Document(path).paragraphs only covers body paragraphs; headers, footers, tables, and text boxes require separate traversal if full-document coverage must be verified
Paragraph alignment (center, left, right: Use python-docx `paragraph.paragraph_format.alignment` and compare against `WD_PARAGRAPH_ALIGNMENT` enum values; note that alignment may be `None` (inheriting from style) rather than an explicit value, so treat `None` as non-centered when checking for explicit center alignment.

When a heading or specific paragraph index is targeted, access `doc.paragraphs[n]` directly; be aware that paragraph index can shift if content is added/removed, so also consider checking by style name via `paragraph.style.name` to locate the correct paragraph.
python-docx reads `.docx` files natively; alignment is stored at the paragraph level in `<w:pPr><w:jc>` XML, which python-docx exposes through `paragraph_format.alignment`.
Export document to PDF: Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract text from each page of the produced PDF and compare against a reference PDF using fuzzy string ratio (fuzz.ratio); a high ratio indicates correct export content.
Check multiple common save locations (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, home directory) with an 'or' conjunction, since the user may choose different export destinations.
Verify the exported PDF retains the original filename stem (only extension changes to .pdf), not a renamed file.
Insert table (rows × columns): Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; verify count, row count (len(table.rows)), and column count (len(table.columns)) match expectations.
Compare cell text with table.cell(i,j).text.strip() across all rows and columns to confirm cell content equality between result and reference documents.
Text highlight color (character backgrou: Use odfpy to parse .odt files: iterate over Span elements, retrieve their 'stylename' attribute, then look up matching automatic styles and check child property nodes for 'backgroundcolor' attribute (e.g., '#ffff00' for yellow) to detect remaining highlights.
Highlight is stored as a character-level automatic style property (backgroundcolor), not a paragraph property, so check automaticstyles childNodes rather than paragraph styles.

compare_docx_files (or equivalent structural comparison) can be used as a preliminary check before inspecting highlight properties, ensuring overall document structure matches before diving into style attributes.
Use python-docx to inspect run.font.highlight_color for each run in paragraphs; highlight colors are WD_COLOR_INDEX enum values (e.g., YELLOW), not RGB—check the enum value rather than an RGB tuple.
When a word like a keyword appears mid-sentence, it may be split across multiple runs; iterate all runs in a paragraph and check both run.text content and run.font.highlight_color together.
compare_docx_files_and_ignore_new_lines only checks paragraph text equality, not formatting—highlight verification requires a separate run-level inspection of font.highlight_color.
Insert image into document: Use python-docx Document.part.rels to extract embedded image blobs; compare count and pixel-level content (Image.tobytes()) between result and reference docx to verify correct image insertion.

Images are stored as relationship parts in the docx package; iterating doc.part.rels.values() and filtering by 'image' in rel.reltype reliably enumerates all embedded images regardless of paragraph position.

Use python-docx to extract embedded images via doc.part.rels; check that the number of images matches and compare raw pixel bytes (Image.open(img).tobytes()) between result and reference docx to verify image identity.
Remove duplicate lines/records from docu: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all non-empty paragraph texts; parse structured fields by splitting on delimiters to extract the key field (e.g., second CSV column) for uniqueness checks.

Apply three-part validation: (1) subset check — every remaining line must exist in the original document's line set; (2) uniqueness check — the key field must have no duplicates among remaining paragraphs; (3) completeness check — the set of unique key values must match the gold standard's set and line counts must agree.
When comparing sets of extracted field values across processed vs. gold files, set equality is more robust than ordered list comparison since line order may vary.
Strikethrough text formatting: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs[-1] to access the last paragraph; iterate run.font.strike to check strikethrough on each run.
All runs in the target paragraph must have font.strike == True; a single run without it means incomplete formatting.
compare_docx_files can be used as a structural pre-check before inspecting specific font attributes.
Font color applied to text runs in table: Use python-docx to iterate document.tables → rows → cells → paragraphs → runs; check run.font.color.rgb against expected RGBColor values
For perceptual color comparison, convert RGB to Lab and use deltaE_ciede2000 (from colormath or skimage) rather than exact RGB equality, with a threshold around 3–4 CIEDE2000 units
When coloring is conditional on word content (e.g., first letter), verify the logic by grouping runs by their text's first character and asserting the corresponding color family (red vs. blue)
compare_docx_files can be used as a structural pre-check before inspecting per-run color attributes
Insert empty paragraph lines between sen: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract the full paragraph list including empty ones; compare paragraph count and text sequence against a reference, since empty lines appear as paragraphs with empty text (p.text == '')

The compare_docx_files metric with ignore_blanks=False does a strict paragraph-by-paragraph count and text match, so both the number of paragraphs and their exact text must match the gold file; use this approach when verifying empty-line insertion tasks
Multiple gold files may represent equivalent valid solutions (e.g., different sentence-splitting strategies); use an 'or' conjunction across compare_docx_files calls to accept any valid variant
When checking empty-line separation, verify that empty paragraphs (p.text.strip() == '') appear at the correct positions between content paragraphs, not just that the total count is right

compare_docx_files_and_ignore_new_lines with ignore_blanks=False checks that blank paragraphs exist at expected positions; blank paragraphs have p.text == '' and are filtered out when ignore_blanks=True, so the option choice affects whether separator lines are validated.
Convert comma-separated text to table: Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; compare table count, row count, and column count between result and reference documents.
Compare cell text with table.cell(i,j).text.strip() for each row/column index to verify correct mapping of comma-delimited values into table cells.
When multiple valid gold references exist (e.g., different column arrangements), use an 'or' conjunction across compare_docx_tables calls so any acceptable layout passes.
Append reference entry to reference list: Use python-docx paragraph text extraction to verify the new reference string appears verbatim in the document's paragraph list; compare_docx_files with ignore_blanks=True collapses whitespace, so minor spacing differences are tolerated.
When the reference list is numbered, check that the new entry carries the correct sequential number prefix as plain text within the paragraph.
Insert cross-reference (by reference num: compare_docx_files compares full paragraph text including inline cross-reference markers; verify the target paragraph contains the bracketed or superscript reference number at the marked location by checking p.text of the relevant paragraph.

Cross-references inserted via LibreOffice may be stored as field codes (REF fields) or as plain text; python-docx exposes run-level text so iterate runs within the paragraph to confirm the reference number token is present regardless of field encoding.
Fuzzy matching (fuzz.ratio) is useful here because field-based cross-references may render slightly differently; a high similarity threshold (≥0.95) is a reliable signal.
Convert uppercase text to lowercase (cas: Use python-docx to extract paragraph texts and compare against a gold document; the compare_docx_files pattern (joining paragraphs, normalizing whitespace) is the standard metric here.

When verifying case transformation, extract all paragraph texts via doc.paragraphs and check that no uppercase characters remain where they should be lowercase; a direct string comparison against a gold .docx is the most reliable approach.
python-docx's p.text aggregates all runs in a paragraph, so run-level case changes are captured without iterating individual runs.
Font size applied to text runs with spec: Use python-docx to iterate document.paragraphs and each paragraph's runs; check run.italic to filter italic runs, then verify run.font.size.pt for the expected size — note that run.font.size may be None if size is inherited rather than explicitly set on the run, so always guard with a None check before accessing .pt

When verifying character-level formatting changes scoped to a style (italic, bold, etc.), iterate all runs across all paragraphs rather than relying on paragraph-level styles, since the formatting is stored at the run level in python-docx
compare_docx_files can be used as a structural pre-check before inspecting individual run properties, to catch gross document-level differences early
Title case (capitalize each word) text t: Use python-docx to extract paragraph texts and compare against expected title-cased content; the compare_docx_files metric collapses whitespace and does exact string matching by default, so verify that every word's first letter is uppercase and remaining letters match the expected casing.

When checking title-case transformations, iterate over all paragraphs (doc.paragraphs) and inspect p.text; be aware that runs within a paragraph may split words, so reconstructing full paragraph text is more reliable than run-level inspection.

compare_docx_files with default options (ignore_blanks=True) normalizes whitespace before comparing, so minor spacing differences won't cause failures, but case differences will — use this to confirm title-case was applied correctly.
Insert page break: Use python-docx to iterate all paragraphs and their runs, searching for `w:br` elements with `w:type='page'` attribute to count explicit page breaks; compare total count against expected value.

Page breaks inserted via LibreOffice Writer appear as `w:br` elements inside run XML (`run.element.findall('.//w:br', namespaces)`), not as paragraph properties, so check run-level XML rather than paragraph-level `pPr`.
Set default font (typeface) for Writer: Parse registrymodifications.xcu with xml.etree.ElementTree; look for item[@oor:path='/org.openoffice.Office.Writer/DefaultFont'] then prop[@oor:name='Standard']/value to retrieve the configured default font name.
The namespace prefix 'oor' maps to 'http://openoffice.org/2001/registry'; always pass the namespace dict to findall/find calls when querying this file.
This setting is stored per-user in ~/.config/libreoffice/4/user/registrymodifications.xcu, not in the document itself, so verification reads that config file rather than any .odt/.docx.
Force quit / terminate LibreOffice Write: Use `ps aux | grep soffice` (with bracket trick to exclude grep itself) to confirm the process is no longer running after the kill command.
Check `~/.bash_history` for a kill-family command (kill, killall, pkill) to verify the user performed the action from the terminal rather than through the GUI.
Combine process-absence check and bash-history check with include/exclude string rules on a single shell command output for atomic pass/fail evaluation.
Save/export text content to Word (.docx): Use python-docx's Document class to read paragraph texts from .docx files; compare with ignore_blanks by collapsing whitespace via re.sub before equality check.
The compare_docx_files pattern extracts all paragraph texts as a flat list, joins them, and normalizes whitespace — useful for plain-text content comparison without caring about paragraph boundaries.
fuzzy matching via fuzz.ratio is available as a fallback when exact text match is too strict; consider it for notes content that may have minor whitespace differences.
python-docx Document() can open and parse .docx files for structural verification; check both paragraph text and run-level formatting attributes after saving.
Batch convert .doc files to PDF via comm: Check bash history for a command matching `(soffice|libreoffice).+--convert-to\s+pdf.+\*.doc` to confirm the batch conversion was invoked correctly
Use `compare_archive` with `file_type='pdf'` to compare the set of produced PDF files against a reference archive; verify both filenames and PDF content match

The `compare_pdfs` function is used internally by `compare_archive` for PDF file type; it compares rendered PDF content, so structural/content fidelity of the conversion is checked, not just file existence
Insert/type text content into document b: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts; compare with expected using whitespace-normalized string comparison (re.sub r'\s+' -> ' ').strip(), which is what compare_docx_files with ignore_blanks=True does
fuzzy_match via fuzz.ratio can catch near-correct answers; for exact title matching, exact string equality after whitespace normalization is the standard check
compare_docx_files_and_ignore_new_lines compares paragraph text after stripping blank paragraphs; with ignore_blanks=False it also checks paragraph count equality, so paragraph structure matters.
When pasting content from JSON values, verify that each value maps to exactly one paragraph and that paragraph text matches the source string character-for-character.
Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts; compare with expected content using ignore_blanks and ignore_case normalization via re.sub(r'\s+',' ') before equality check
When order-insensitive comparison is needed, sort both paragraph lists before comparing; fuzz.ratio from rapidfuzz/thefuzz can handle near-match scoring
Read instructions from a Writer document: This task is evaluated entirely on the resulting spreadsheet (xlsx), not on the Writer document itself; use compare_table with sheet_data rules via openpyxl/pandas to verify cell values across all sheets.
Insert table with data extracted from ex: Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; compare count, row/column dimensions, and cell text between result and reference documents — compare_docx_tables pattern covers all these checks in one pass
When verifying table cell content, strip whitespace from both sides before comparing to avoid false mismatches from trailing newlines or spaces

Table position within the document (e.g., under a specific heading) is not checked by compare_docx_tables; only table count and cell content are validated, so placement verification requires inspecting paragraph order relative to tables if needed
Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; compare row/column counts and cell text (stripped) against a reference docx to verify structural and content fidelity
compare_docx_tables pattern: iterate zip(tables1,tables2), check len(rows)==len(rows) and len(columns)==len(columns), then cell(i,j).text.strip() equality for every cell
When transferring spreadsheet data to a Writer table, verify the table dimensions match the source sheet's used range (rows × columns) and that numeric/text cell values are preserved exactly
Insert speaker notes into presentation s: Use python-pptx: slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text to retrieve note content; compare stripped text against expected value per slide

The compare_pptx_files evaluator checks notes via get_slide_notes(slide).strip() != get_slide_notes(slide2).strip() with examine_note=True by default; ensure note text matches exactly after stripping whitespace

When reading speaking notes from a Writer document to populate Impress slide notes, verify the correct mapping of note text to slide index by iterating prs.slides and checking each slide's notes_text_frame
File classification and organization int: Use vm_command_line with `ls` on each target directory and compare the exact sorted output string (including trailing newline) against expected filenames; exact_match is strict so order and whitespace matter.
When files lack clear extensions, content analysis (reading file text/metadata) is needed to classify them; verify by checking presence/absence of files across all category folders, not just one.
Verify all three category folders (e.g., Paper_reading, Projects, Miscellaneous) together to ensure no file is missing or misplaced across the full set.
Append formatted answer content to exist: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts and compare against a gold .docx file; the compare_docx_files metric collapses whitespace and optionally ignores case, so focus on logical text content equality rather than exact whitespace

When a task requires replicating an existing format (e.g., answer list structure), verify by comparing paragraph-level text of the result doc against a reference doc using fuzz.ratio or exact match after whitespace normalization

python-docx paragraph iteration covers the full document body; tables and other non-paragraph elements are not captured by doc.paragraphs, so if answers are in tables use doc.tables[i].rows[j].cells[k].text instead
Load both candidate and gold .docx with python-docx, extract paragraph texts, normalize whitespace, and compare as joined strings; ignore_order option is useful when entry sequence may differ
For structured list entries (e.g., paper metadata blocks), sorting paragraphs before comparison handles insertion-order variance without losing correctness signal
Extract and transfer text from Impress p: Use python-docx to read paragraph texts from the output .docx and compare against expected content; the compare_docx_files metric uses fuzz.ratio on joined paragraph text with ignore_blanks, ignore_order, content_only, and delete_empty_lines options, so focus on text content rather than formatting

When verifying cross-app text extraction (Impress→Writer), extract all text frames/shapes from the .pptx/.odp source using python-pptx or odfpy and confirm each text string appears in the Writer document paragraphs

The evaluator collapses whitespace with re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', ...) before comparing, so minor spacing differences are tolerated; verify that all non-empty text blocks are present rather than exact paragraph structure
Read algorithm instructions from Writer: Use compare_text_file metric on the output text file; exact string match (after strip) is required unless ignore_blanks/ignore_case options are set
When a task requires reading a .docx for coding instructions, verify the output file content matches a gold reference file byte-for-byte (post-strip); no partial-credit path exists with this metric
Package/zip files for submission accordi: Use Python's zipfile module to compare zip contents: verify both the set of filenames (namelist) and byte-level content of each entry match the reference zip; for PDF entries inside the zip, use a fuzzy PDF text-content comparison (e.g., extract text with pdfminer/PyMuPDF and compare with a similarity threshold) rather than byte equality, since PDF rendering can vary slightly across runs.
Capture terminal screenshot for document: Use easyocr (compare_image_text metric) to verify screenshot content by OCR-extracting text and checking for expected substrings; account for OCR misreads (e.g., 'ls' vs '1s') by accepting alternative OCR renderings as valid matches

Image files may be saved in X11 screen dump (xwd) format rather than true PNG even with a .png extension; verify format with subprocess 'file' command and convert via PIL, custom X11 reader, or netpbm tools before OCR
When verifying screenshot content, use substring matching on the full joined OCR text rather than exact equality, since OCR output order and spacing vary
Read image editing instructions from Wri: Use SSIM (structural similarity index) via skimage.metrics to compare grayscale versions of the output image against a reference; resize both to the smaller dimension before comparison to handle minor size differences.
When instructions are embedded in a Writer document, parse the document text (e.g., via python-docx or LibreOffice UNO) to extract editing parameters rather than hard-coding them.

Image comparison metrics like SSIM are sensitive to both structural content and pixel-level changes; a base_score reference pattern is sometimes used so only improvements above a threshold count as correct.
Merge/concatenate multiple text files in: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts and compare against a reference docx; the compare_docx_files metric normalizes whitespace (re.sub r'\s+') before comparing, so focus on logical text content equality rather than exact whitespace.
When merging files without separators, verify that paragraph text from all source files appears contiguously in the output docx with no extra blank-line paragraphs between them.
compare_docx_files with ignore_blanks=True collapses all whitespace, so minor spacing differences won't cause failure; content order and completeness are the critical checks.
Font size applied to entire document (gl: Check document-level default font size via doc.styles['Default Paragraph Style'] or doc.styles['Normal'] style's font.size attribute in python-docx; individual run-level font sizes may override this.

Iterate all runs across all paragraphs and verify run.font.size is consistent with the target pt value (python-docx stores size in EMUs: pt * 12700); runs inheriting from style may have font.size == None, meaning they use the style default.
Also inspect the document's default character style and paragraph style font size to confirm the global setting, not just individual run overrides.
Read paper references from Writer docume: Use compare_text_file with ignore_blanks=True to normalize whitespace differences; exact BibTeX field order and blank-line separators are collapsed, so content equality is what matters

When checking BibTeX entries, prefer published venue entries over arXiv preprint entries for the same paper — verify that @article/@inproceedings entries are used rather than @misc with eprint fields when a published version exists
DBLP BibTeX keys and field values must match the canonical DBLP record; compare against a gold .bib file using text comparison rather than parsing the BibTeX structure
Split document into multiple chapter PDF: Use compare_archive with file_type='pdf' to compare sets of per-chapter PDF files; filenames must match exactly (sorted comparison), so verify naming convention matches the established example before exporting
compare_pdfs is used internally; PDF content comparison checks rendered page content, so chapter boundaries (page ranges) must be correct, not just file count
When splitting a multi-chapter document, each exported PDF should contain only its respective chapter's pages; verify page count per PDF matches expected chapter length

The archive comparison first checks that pred_files == gold_files (exact filename match including order); naming pattern derived from the existing chapter-one example must be followed precisely for all subsequent chapters
Save text content to Writer document: Use python-docx's Document class to read .docx files; iterate doc.paragraphs and collect para.text to get all written content

When verifying multi-item list content (e.g., addresses), split paragraph text on whitespace and use fuzzy string matching (e.g., fuzz.ratio) against a set of acceptable answers rather than exact equality, since formatting may vary
Score-based evaluation: compute per-token fuzzy match scores against an expected list, threshold low scores to zero, and normalize by the expected item count to get a partial-credit float metric
Use file read + text normalization (expand tabs, strip trailing whitespace, drop empty lines) before comparing; shebang/encoding header lines at file start may be skipped safely.
Compare normalized line-by-line content rather than raw byte equality to tolerate minor whitespace differences.
Python file content comparison should preserve indentation and inline comments; only strip truly empty lines and file-level metadata headers.
Chrome extension installation via Web St: Read installed extension names from the Chrome Preferences JSON file (path varies by OS/architecture) under extensions.settings.<id>.manifest.name; use this list for subset-membership checks rather than exact equality.
Normalize extension name aliases (e.g. alternate store titles for the same extension) before comparing expected vs. installed sets, since store display names can vary across Chrome versions.
Extension installation: Verify extension installation by grepping for the .oxt filename pattern under the LibreOffice user uno_packages cache directory (e.g., /home/user/.config/libreoffice/4/user/uno_packages/cache/uno_packages/); use regex matching on grep output rather than exact path checks.
For extensions with Java dependencies, verify the required JRE/JDK is installed by checking `apt list --installed` output with a regex like `openjdk-\d+-(jre|jdk)`.
Use check_list-style evaluation: collect command stdout to a cache file, then apply regex expect/unexpect rules line-by-line to confirm presence or absence of installation artifacts.
